two-sum.cue: Find a pair with a target sum in an unsorted array, and you need indices: look up the complement in a hash map.
edge: Duplicates that form the pair (`[3,3]`, target 6)
The same index must not be used twice
two-sum.bug: Putting all numbers in the map first, then matching an element with itself. Check the map before inserting.

follow.q: What if the array is sorted?
follow.a: Two pointers from both ends, O(1) extra space.

contains-duplicate.cue: "Has any value been seen before?" is a set-membership question.
contains-duplicate.brute: Compare every pair: O(n²); or sort first, O(n log n).
edge: Large values (do not use a counting array)
contains-duplicate.bug: Sorting the caller's array in place without saying it mutates input.

valid-anagram.cue: Same letters, same counts: compare frequency counts.
valid-anagram.brute: Sort both strings and compare: O(n log n).
edge: Different lengths: return false at once
valid-anagram.bug: Forgetting the length check, so `"ab"` vs `"abc"` passes a one-sided count.

follow.a: Count in a `HashMap<Integer, Integer>` over code points instead of `int[26]`.

group-anagrams.cue: Group items that are equal after normalising: build a canonical key (sorted letters or a 26-count signature).
group-anagrams.brute: Compare every pair of strings for anagram-ness: O(n² · k).
edge: Words of different lengths never match
group-anagrams.bug: Using `char[].toString()` as the key (it prints an object address). Use `new String(chars)` or `Arrays.toString(count)`.

follow.a: A count signature like `#1#0#2...` is O(k) instead of O(k log k).

top-k-frequent-elements.cue: "Top k by frequency": count, then pick k with a min-heap of size k or bucket by frequency.
top-k-frequent-elements.brute: Count, then sort all entries by count: O(n log n).
edge: k equals the number of distinct elements
Ties in frequency (any order is fine)
top-k-frequent-elements.bug: Using a max-heap of all n entries, which is O(n log n) and misses the point of a size-k heap.

follow.q: Can you beat O(n log k)?
follow.a: Bucket sort by frequency (index = count, at most n): O(n).

product-of-array-except-self.cue: "Everything except me" with no division: prefix products from the left times suffix products from the right.
product-of-array-except-self.brute: For each index multiply all the others: O(n²). Division fails on zeros.
edge: One zero (only that index is non-zero)
product-of-array-except-self.bug: Using division, which breaks on zero and is disallowed.

follow.a: Store prefixes in the output array, then multiply in a running suffix in a second pass.

longest-consecutive-sequence.cue: Longest run of consecutive integers in O(n): a hash set, and only start counting at a number whose predecessor is missing.
longest-consecutive-sequence.brute: Sort and scan: O(n log n). Or expand from every number: O(n²).
longest-consecutive-sequence.bug: Expanding from every element instead of only sequence starts, which makes it O(n²).

subarray-sum-equals-k.cue: Count subarrays with sum k when values can be negative: prefix sums plus a map of how often each prefix sum occurred.
edge: Negative numbers (sliding window does not work)
Seed the map with `{0: 1}` for subarrays starting at index 0
subarray-sum-equals-k.bug: Trying a sliding window, which needs all-positive values. Forgetting the `{0: 1}` seed.

follow.a: Store the first index of each prefix sum instead of a count.

maximum-subarray.cue: Best contiguous sum: Kadane's, extend the current run or restart at the current element.
edge: All negative (answer is the largest single element)
maximum-subarray.bug: Starting the best at 0, which returns 0 for an all-negative array.

follow.a: Track where the current run started and copy start/end when the best improves.

sort-colors.cue: Three values to partition in one pass: Dutch national flag with low, mid and high pointers.
sort-colors.brute: Counting sort with two passes, which is fine but they ask for one pass.
sort-colors.bug: Advancing `mid` after swapping with `high`: the swapped-in value has not been checked yet.

majority-element.cue: An element that appears more than n/2 times: Boyer-Moore voting with a candidate and a counter.
majority-element.brute: Count with a hash map: O(n) space. Sort and take the middle: O(n log n).
majority-element.bug: Not verifying the candidate when the problem does not guarantee a majority exists.

follow.a: Do a second pass to count the candidate.

majority-element-ii.cue: More than n/3 times: at most two answers, so keep two candidates with two counters (extended Boyer-Moore).
majority-element-ii.bug: Skipping the verification pass, so a candidate below n/3 is returned.

next-permutation.cue: Next lexicographic arrangement: find the rightmost ascent, swap with the next-larger element to its right, reverse the suffix.
next-permutation.brute: Generate all permutations and sort: O(n!).
next-permutation.bug: Sorting the suffix instead of reversing it (it is already descending, so reversing is O(n)).

merge-sorted-array.cue: Merge into the first array in place: fill from the back so you never overwrite unread values.
merge-sorted-array.bug: Stopping when nums1 is exhausted and forgetting to copy the rest of nums2.

set-matrix-zeroes.cue: Mark rows and columns to clear: in O(1) space use the first row and first column as markers.
set-matrix-zeroes.brute: Copy the matrix, or keep row/column sets: O(m + n) space.
edge: A zero in the first row or column itself
set-matrix-zeroes.bug: Zeroing the first row/column before using them as markers. Record separately whether they had a zero.

rotate-image.cue: Rotate an n×n matrix in place by 90°: transpose, then reverse each row.
rotate-image.brute: Copy into a new matrix: O(n²) extra space.
rotate-image.bug: Transposing the whole matrix instead of only `j > i`, which swaps every pair twice and undoes the transpose.

follow.a: Transpose, then reverse each column (or reverse rows first, then transpose).

spiral-matrix.cue: Layer-by-layer traversal: four boundaries (top, bottom, left, right) that shrink after each side.
spiral-matrix.brute: Simulate with a visited matrix and direction changes: O(m·n) extra space.
spiral-matrix.bug: Not re-checking `top <= bottom` and `left <= right` before the bottom and left passes, which duplicates cells.

best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock.cue: One buy then one sell: track the minimum price so far and the best profit selling today.
best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock.bug: Selling before buying, for example taking max minus min regardless of order.

follow.a: Add every positive day-to-day difference.

valid-sudoku.cue: Check rows, columns and boxes for repeats: one set per unit, box index = `(r / 3) * 3 + c / 3`.
valid-sudoku.brute: Three separate passes, which is fine but wordier.
edge: Only filled cells need to be valid; the board need not be solvable
valid-sudoku.bug: Wrong box index formula, which mixes cells from different boxes.

valid-palindrome.cue: Compare from both ends inward, skipping what does not count.
valid-palindrome.brute: Build a cleaned, reversed copy: O(n) space.
valid-palindrome.bug: Skipping characters with an `if` instead of a `while`, so runs of punctuation break it.

two-sum-ii-input-array-is-sorted.cue: Sorted input plus a pair sum: two pointers, move the side that fixes the sum.
two-sum-ii-input-array-is-sorted.brute: Hash map, which works but ignores the sorted order and uses O(n) space.
two-sum-ii-input-array-is-sorted.bug: Returning 0-based indices when the problem asks for 1-based.

3sum.cue: Triplets summing to zero without duplicates: sort, fix one element, two pointers on the rest.
3sum.brute: Three nested loops plus a set to dedupe: O(n³).
3sum.bug: Deduplicating incorrectly: skip equal fixed elements, and skip equal left/right values only after recording a match.

follow.a: Same skeleton; track the sum with the smallest absolute difference.

4sum.cue: k-sum: sort, fix two elements, two pointers on the rest; dedupe at every level.
edge: Overflow: sums can exceed int, use `long`
4sum.bug: Integer overflow on `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[l] + nums[r]` with large values.

container-with-most-water.cue: Maximise width × min height: start at both ends and move the shorter wall inward.
container-with-most-water.bug: Moving the taller wall; the shorter wall caps the area, so only moving it can help.

trapping-rain-water.cue: Water above a bar = min(max to its left, max to its right) − height: two pointers carrying left and right maxima.
trapping-rain-water.brute: For each bar scan left and right for the maxima: O(n²).
trapping-rain-water.bug: Moving the pointer on the higher side; process the side with the smaller max, because that max is the bound.

follow.q: Can you do it with a stack?
follow.a: Yes: a monotonic decreasing stack fills water layer by layer, also O(n).

remove-duplicates-from-sorted-array.cue: Sorted plus in-place dedupe: a slow write pointer and a fast read pointer.
remove-duplicates-from-sorted-array.brute: Copy uniques into a new list: O(n) space.
remove-duplicates-from-sorted-array.bug: Returning the last index instead of the new length.

move-zeroes.cue: Stable in-place partition: write non-zeros forward, then fill the tail with zeros (or swap).
move-zeroes.brute: Copy into a new array: O(n) space.
move-zeroes.bug: Breaking the relative order of the non-zero elements.

longest-substring-without-repeating-char.cue: Longest contiguous stretch with a constraint: variable sliding window, shrink when a character repeats.
longest-substring-without-repeating-char.brute: Check every substring: O(n²) to O(n³).
edge: Spaces and symbols count as characters
longest-substring-without-repeating-char.bug: Jumping `left` backwards with `left = last[c] + 1`; use `max(left, last[c] + 1)`.

follow.a: Same window; shrink while the map holds more than k keys.

longest-repeating-character-replacement.cue: Window that is valid while `length − maxFreq ≤ k`.
longest-repeating-character-replacement.brute: Try every substring and count: O(n²).
longest-repeating-character-replacement.bug: Recomputing maxFreq on every shrink; it never needs to decrease for the answer to be correct.

permutation-in-string.cue: Does a substring of s2 have the same counts as s1? A fixed-size window of length |s1| comparing counts.
permutation-in-string.bug: Comparing whole maps every step; compare `int[26]` arrays or keep a match counter.

minimum-window-substring.cue: Smallest window containing all of t (with counts): expand until valid, then shrink while still valid.
minimum-window-substring.brute: Every substring checked against t: O(n²·m).
minimum-window-substring.bug: Counting distinct characters instead of required counts, so `t = "aa"` matches a single `a`.

follow.q: Return the count of such windows?
follow.a: Every extension to the right of a minimal valid window is also valid; count as you shrink.

sliding-window-maximum.cue: Max of every window of size k: a monotonic deque of indices, decreasing values, front is the max.
sliding-window-maximum.brute: Scan each window: O(n·k). A heap: O(n log n).
sliding-window-maximum.bug: Storing values instead of indices, so you cannot tell when the front left the window.

max-consecutive-ones-iii.cue: Longest window with at most k zeros: variable window counting zeros.
max-consecutive-ones-iii.bug: Flipping values in the array instead of counting zeros in the window.

fruit-into-baskets.cue: Longest subarray with at most 2 distinct values: variable window with a count map.
fruit-into-baskets.bug: Forgetting to remove a key when its count drops to 0, so the distinct count is wrong.

minimum-size-subarray-sum.cue: Shortest subarray with sum ≥ target, all positive: grow, then shrink while the sum is enough.
minimum-size-subarray-sum.bug: Using this window on arrays with negatives; it needs positive values (otherwise prefix sums plus a deque).

valid-parentheses.cue: Matching nested pairs: push openers, pop on closers.
valid-parentheses.brute: Repeatedly remove `()`, `[]`, `{}` from the string: O(n²).
valid-parentheses.bug: Returning true without checking the stack is empty at the end.

min-stack.cue: O(1) minimum with push/pop: keep a second stack (or pairs) holding the minimum at each depth.
min-stack.brute: Scan the stack for the minimum: O(n).
min-stack.bug: Pushing to the min stack only on a strictly smaller value, so popping a duplicate minimum loses it.

evaluate-reverse-polish-notation.cue: Postfix expression: operands on a stack, apply each operator to the top two.
evaluate-reverse-polish-notation.brute: There is no simpler alternative; the stack is the solution.
evaluate-reverse-polish-notation.bug: Wrong operand order: pop `b` first, then `a`, and compute `a - b` and `a / b`.

daily-temperatures.cue: "Next greater element to the right": a monotonic decreasing stack of indices.
daily-temperatures.brute: For each day scan forward: O(n²).
edge: Equal temperatures do not count as warmer
daily-temperatures.bug: Popping on `>=`, which treats equal temperatures as warmer.

next-greater-element-i.cue: Next greater for each value of nums2 with a monotonic stack, then look up nums1 values in a map.
next-greater-element-i.brute: For each query scan nums2: O(n·m).
edge: nums1 is a subset of nums2 with distinct values
next-greater-element-i.bug: Running the stack over nums1 instead of nums2.

largest-rectangle-in-histogram.cue: For each bar, how far can it extend left and right? A monotonic increasing stack gives both boundaries.
edge: Add a 0-height sentinel at the end to flush the stack
largest-rectangle-in-histogram.bug: Wrong width: after popping, the width is `i - stack.peek() - 1`, or `i` when the stack is empty.

follow.q: Maximal rectangle of 1s in a matrix?
follow.a: Build a histogram per row and run this algorithm on each row: O(m·n).

car-fleet.cue: Sort by position and compare arrival times from the front: a car that would arrive sooner than the one ahead joins its fleet.
car-fleet.brute: Simulate time steps: slow and fiddly.
edge: Cars arriving at exactly the same time form one fleet
car-fleet.bug: Sorting by speed or by arrival time instead of by position.

asteroid-collision.cue: Only a left-mover meeting a right-mover collides: simulate with a stack.
edge: A left-mover with nothing to its left survives
asteroid-collision.bug: Treating `-` followed by `+` as a collision; they move apart.

online-stock-span.cue: Consecutive previous days with price ≤ today: a monotonic stack of (price, span) pairs, merging spans.
online-stock-span.brute: Walk back each day: O(n) per call, O(n²) in total.
online-stock-span.bug: Storing only prices, so you lose the accumulated span of popped days.

binary-search.cue: Sorted array plus find: halve the search space.
edge: Target smaller or larger than all elements
binary-search.bug: `mid = (lo + hi) / 2` overflows for large indices; use `lo + (hi - lo) / 2`. Mixing `<` and `<=` loop styles.

search-a-2d-matrix.cue: Rows sorted and each row starts after the previous ends: treat it as one sorted array of m·n.
search-a-2d-matrix.bug: Wrong index mapping: `row = mid / cols`, `col = mid % cols`.

search-in-rotated-sorted-array.cue: Rotated sorted array: one half around mid is always sorted; check whether the target lies in it.
search-in-rotated-sorted-array.brute: Linear scan: O(n). Or find the pivot first, then search (two passes).
search-in-rotated-sorted-array.bug: Using strict `<` when checking which half is sorted, which breaks when `lo == mid`.

follow.a: When `nums[lo] == nums[mid] == nums[hi]` you cannot tell, so shrink both ends; worst case O(n).

find-minimum-in-rotated-sorted-array.cue: Compare mid with the right end: if larger, the minimum is to the right.
find-minimum-in-rotated-sorted-array.bug: Comparing with the left end, which fails when the array is not rotated.

find-first-and-last-position-of-element-.cue: Two binary searches for boundaries: lower bound of target and lower bound of target + 1.
find-first-and-last-position-of-element-.brute: Find one occurrence, then expand: O(n) in the worst case.
find-first-and-last-position-of-element-.bug: Stopping at the first match instead of continuing left (or right) to the boundary.

koko-eating-bananas.cue: "Minimum speed or capacity such that a condition holds": binary search on the answer with a feasibility check.
koko-eating-bananas.brute: Try every speed from 1 upwards: O(max · n).
edge: h equals the number of piles (answer is the max pile)
koko-eating-bananas.bug: Hours per pile as `p / k` instead of the ceiling `(p + k - 1) / k`.

capacity-to-ship-packages-within-d-days.cue: Minimise the maximum load: binary search capacity between max(weight) and sum(weights).
capacity-to-ship-packages-within-d-days.bug: Lower bound of 1 instead of max(weights), so a package can never ship.

split-array-largest-sum.cue: "Split into k parts minimising the largest part": the same binary search on the answer as shipping packages.
split-array-largest-sum.brute: DP over split points: O(k · n²).
split-array-largest-sum.bug: Counting parts wrongly: start the count at 1, and add one each time the running sum would exceed the limit.

find-peak-element.cue: Any peak in O(log n): move toward the larger neighbour, a peak must exist on that side.
find-peak-element.bug: Accessing `mid + 1` out of bounds; loop `while (lo < hi)`.

time-based-key-value-store.cue: Latest value at or before a timestamp: per key, a list sorted by time plus binary search (or a `TreeMap.floorEntry`).
time-based-key-value-store.brute: Scan all versions of the key: O(n) per get.
edge: Query earlier than the first set ("")
time-based-key-value-store.bug: Searching for an exact timestamp instead of the floor.

median-of-two-sorted-arrays.cue: Binary search the partition of the shorter array so both left halves together hold half the elements.
median-of-two-sorted-arrays.brute: Merge, then take the middle: O(m + n).
edge: Partitions at the very ends (use ±∞ sentinels)
median-of-two-sorted-arrays.bug: Searching the longer array, which can push the other partition out of range.

reverse-linked-list.cue: Reverse pointers in place with prev, cur and next.
reverse-linked-list.brute: Copy values to a list and rebuild: O(n) space.
reverse-linked-list.bug: Losing the rest of the list by overwriting `cur.next` before saving it.

follow.a: Reverse the rest, then `head.next.next = head; head.next = null`. O(n) stack.

merge-two-sorted-lists.cue: Merge step of merge sort with a dummy head.
merge-two-sorted-lists.brute: Collect, sort, rebuild: O(n log n).
merge-two-sorted-lists.bug: Forgetting to attach the remaining tail of the longer list.

linked-list-cycle.cue: Cycle detection in O(1) space: slow and fast pointers.
linked-list-cycle.brute: Hash set of visited nodes: O(n) space.
linked-list-cycle.bug: Checking `fast.next.next` without checking `fast.next` first, giving a NullPointerException.

linked-list-cycle-ii.cue: After slow and fast meet, a pointer from head and one from the meeting point meet at the cycle start.
linked-list-cycle-ii.brute: Hash set of visited nodes: O(n) space.
linked-list-cycle-ii.bug: Not being able to explain why it works: distance head→start equals distance meeting→start modulo the cycle length.

follow.a: From the meeting point, walk until you return and count the steps.

remove-nth-node-from-end-of-list.cue: n-th from the end in one pass: fast pointer n steps ahead, then move both.
remove-nth-node-from-end-of-list.brute: Count the length, then walk again: two passes.
remove-nth-node-from-end-of-list.bug: No dummy node, so removing the head needs a special case.

reorder-list.cue: Three known steps: find the middle, reverse the second half, merge alternately.
reorder-list.brute: Copy nodes into an array and relink: O(n) space.
reorder-list.bug: Not cutting the first half (`mid.next = null`), which leaves a cycle.

add-two-numbers.cue: Digit-by-digit addition with carry over reversed lists.
add-two-numbers.brute: Convert to numbers: overflows for long lists.
edge: Final carry creates a new node (5 + 5)

follow.a: Use two stacks, or reverse both lists first.

copy-list-with-random-pointer.cue: Deep copy with extra pointers: a map old→new, or interleave copies to get O(1) space.
copy-list-with-random-pointer.brute: There is no meaningful brute force; the map version is the baseline.
copy-list-with-random-pointer.bug: Not restoring the original list in the interleaving version.

lru-cache.cue: O(1) get and put with eviction by recency: hash map plus doubly linked list.
lru-cache.brute: A list scanned on every access: O(n).
edge: put on an existing key updates and refreshes it
lru-cache.bug: Forgetting to delete the evicted key from the map, or not refreshing recency on get.

follow.a: A lock around get/put (both mutate order), or segmented locks; `LinkedHashMap` + `synchronized` is the simple answer.

merge-k-sorted-lists.cue: k sorted streams: a min-heap of the current heads.
merge-k-sorted-lists.brute: Merge one list at a time: O(N·k).
merge-k-sorted-lists.bug: Adding null heads to the priority queue.

follow.a: Divide and conquer: merge pairs, O(N log k) with no extra space besides recursion.

reverse-nodes-in-k-group.cue: Reverse fixed-size chunks: check k nodes exist, reverse them, reconnect to the previous group.
reverse-nodes-in-k-group.brute: Copy to an array and rebuild: O(n) space.
edge: Length not divisible by k (leave the tail)
reverse-nodes-in-k-group.bug: Losing the connection between groups; keep `groupPrev` and the next group's head.

palindrome-linked-list.cue: O(1) space: find the middle, reverse the second half, compare.
palindrome-linked-list.brute: Copy into an array: O(n) space.
palindrome-linked-list.bug: Not restoring the list when the caller expects it unchanged.

intersection-of-two-linked-lists.cue: Two pointers that switch to the other list's head equalise the lengths.
intersection-of-two-linked-lists.brute: Hash set of one list's nodes: O(n) space.
intersection-of-two-linked-lists.bug: Comparing values instead of node references.

maximum-depth-of-binary-tree.cue: Height = 1 + max of the children's heights.
maximum-depth-of-binary-tree.brute: Already optimal; BFS counting levels also works.

invert-binary-tree.cue: Swap children at every node (any traversal).

same-tree.cue: Structural recursion: equal values plus equal left and right subtrees.
same-tree.brute: Serialise both and compare strings: more memory.
same-tree.bug: Not handling the one-null case before reading `.val`.

subtree-of-another-tree.brute: This is the simple version: O(n·m). Serialise with null markers plus string matching gives O(n + m).
edge: subRoot equal to the whole tree
subtree-of-another-tree.bug: Serialising without null markers or delimiters, so `12` matches `2`.

diameter-of-binary-tree.cue: Longest path through a node = left height + right height; update a global maximum during the height recursion.
diameter-of-binary-tree.brute: Compute heights separately at every node: O(n²).
edge: Longest path not through the root
diameter-of-binary-tree.bug: Returning the diameter from the recursion instead of the height.

follow.a: Same recursion, add edge weights instead of 1.

balanced-binary-tree.cue: Return the height or -1 for unbalanced, so each node is visited once.
balanced-binary-tree.brute: Compute heights at every node: O(n²).
edge: Balanced at the root but not deeper
balanced-binary-tree.bug: Checking balance only at the root.

binary-tree-level-order-traversal.cue: Level by level: BFS with the queue size frozen at the start of each level.
binary-tree-level-order-traversal.bug: Reading `queue.size()` inside the loop, so the level mixes nodes.

binary-tree-right-side-view.cue: Last node of each BFS level (or DFS right-first, first visit at each depth).
binary-tree-right-side-view.brute: Collect all levels, then take the last of each: same complexity, more memory.
edge: Left nodes visible where the right subtree is shorter
binary-tree-right-side-view.bug: Following only right children, which misses left nodes in deeper levels.

binary-tree-zigzag-level-order-traversal.cue: Level-order BFS, reversing the direction of every other level.
binary-tree-zigzag-level-order-traversal.brute: Reverse alternate lists afterwards: fine, slightly more work.
binary-tree-zigzag-level-order-traversal.bug: Changing the child insertion order instead of the output order, which scrambles later levels.

lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-searc.cue: BST ordering: the LCA is the first node whose value lies between p and q.
edge: p is an ancestor of q
lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-searc.bug: Ignoring the BST property and doing a full search.

lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-tree.cue: Post-order: if p and q are found in different subtrees, the current node is the LCA.
lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-tree.brute: Store both root-to-node paths and compare: O(n) extra space.
edge: One node is an ancestor of the other
lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-tree.bug: Stopping early without understanding that returning the found node covers the ancestor case.

follow.a: Walk up from both like the linked-list intersection problem.

validate-binary-search-tree.cue: Every node must lie within (min, max) bounds inherited from its ancestors, or in-order must be strictly increasing.
validate-binary-search-tree.brute: Check only parent-child pairs, which is wrong rather than slow.
validate-binary-search-tree.bug: Comparing a node only with its direct children.

kth-smallest-element-in-a-bst.cue: In-order traversal of a BST is sorted: stop at the k-th node.
kth-smallest-element-in-a-bst.brute: Collect all values and sort: O(n log n).
kth-smallest-element-in-a-bst.bug: Traversing the whole tree after finding the answer.

follow.a: Store subtree sizes in each node for O(h) per query.

construct-binary-tree-from-preorder-and-.cue: Preorder gives the root; its position in inorder splits the left and right subtrees.
construct-binary-tree-from-preorder-and-.brute: Search inorder linearly for each root: O(n²).
construct-binary-tree-from-preorder-and-.bug: Linear search for the root in inorder; use a value→index map.

binary-tree-maximum-path-sum.cue: At each node: best downward gain = val + max(0, left, right); the path through the node uses both sides.
binary-tree-maximum-path-sum.brute: Try every pair of endpoints: O(n²).
edge: All negative values (answer is the largest single node)
binary-tree-maximum-path-sum.bug: Not clamping negative child gains to 0, or initialising the answer to 0.

serialize-and-deserialize-binary-tree.cue: Preorder with null markers is enough to rebuild the tree uniquely.
serialize-and-deserialize-binary-tree.brute: Level order with nulls also works; both are O(n).
serialize-and-deserialize-binary-tree.bug: Omitting null markers, which makes the structure ambiguous.

count-good-nodes-in-binary-tree.cue: DFS carrying the maximum seen on the path from the root.
count-good-nodes-in-binary-tree.brute: Store each root-to-node path: more memory.

binary-tree-inorder-traversal.cue: Iterative in-order: push left children, pop, visit, go right.
binary-tree-inorder-traversal.brute: Recursion is the baseline; they usually ask for the iterative version.
binary-tree-inorder-traversal.bug: Pushing the right child before visiting the node.

maximum-width-of-binary-tree.cue: BFS with position indices (left = 2i, right = 2i + 1); width = last − first + 1 per level.
maximum-width-of-binary-tree.brute: Fill missing nodes with placeholders: exponential.
edge: Index overflow in deep skewed trees: re-base indices per level
maximum-width-of-binary-tree.bug: Letting indices grow without re-basing, which overflows.

all-nodes-distance-k-in-binary-tree.cue: Distance in a tree means moving up too: add parent links (make it a graph), then BFS from the target.
all-nodes-distance-k-in-binary-tree.brute: Without parent links you need case analysis per ancestor.
all-nodes-distance-k-in-binary-tree.bug: Not tracking visited nodes, so BFS walks back down.

flatten-binary-tree-to-linked-list.cue: Preorder order in place: for each node, attach the left subtree between it and its right subtree.
flatten-binary-tree-to-linked-list.brute: Collect preorder into a list and relink: O(n) space.

implement-trie-prefix-tree.cue: Prefix queries over many words: a tree of characters with an end-of-word flag.
implement-trie-prefix-tree.brute: A list of words scanned per query: O(n·L).
edge: A word that is a prefix of another
implement-trie-prefix-tree.bug: Making `search` return true for a prefix by not checking the end flag.

design-add-and-search-words-data-structu.cue: Trie plus DFS that branches on `.` wildcards.
design-add-and-search-words-data-structu.brute: Compare against every stored word: O(n·L).
design-add-and-search-words-data-structu.bug: Returning early on the first wildcard branch that fails instead of trying all children.

word-search-ii.cue: Many words in one grid: put the words in a trie and DFS the grid once.
word-search-ii.brute: Run Word Search for each word: O(words · m·n·4^L).
word-search-ii.bug: Not pruning: remove found words or empty trie branches, otherwise it times out.

maximum-xor-of-two-numbers-in-an-array.cue: Maximise XOR bit by bit from the top: a binary trie, prefer the opposite bit.
maximum-xor-of-two-numbers-in-an-array.bug: Iterating bits from low to high; greedy only works from the most significant bit.

kth-largest-element-in-a-stream.cue: k-th largest over a stream: a min-heap of size k, its top is the answer.
kth-largest-element-in-a-stream.brute: Sort on every add: O(n log n) per call.

last-stone-weight.cue: Repeatedly take the two largest: a max-heap.
last-stone-weight.brute: Sort every round: O(n² log n).

k-closest-points-to-origin.cue: k smallest by distance: a max-heap of size k (or quickselect).
k-closest-points-to-origin.brute: Sort all points: O(n log n).
k-closest-points-to-origin.bug: Using `Math.sqrt` (unnecessary) or squared distances that overflow `int` with large coordinates.

kth-largest-element-in-an-array.cue: k-th order statistic: a size-k min-heap, or quickselect for O(n) on average.
kth-largest-element-in-an-array.bug: Quickselect without a random pivot, which degrades to O(n²) on sorted input.

follow.a: Median of medians, but say quickselect with a random pivot is what is used in practice.

find-median-from-data-stream.cue: Median of a stream: a max-heap for the lower half, a min-heap for the upper half, kept balanced.
find-median-from-data-stream.brute: Sort on every query: O(n log n).
find-median-from-data-stream.bug: Not rebalancing after each insert, so the heaps differ by more than one.

follow.a: A counting array gives O(100) per median.

top-k-frequent-words.cue: Top k with a tie-break: a heap with comparator (count desc, word asc).
top-k-frequent-words.brute: Sort all words: O(n log n), which is acceptable but not the expected answer.
edge: k equals the number of distinct words
top-k-frequent-words.bug: Getting the comparator backwards in the size-k min-heap, then not reversing the result.

reorganize-string.cue: Place the most frequent characters first, never the same one twice in a row: a max-heap by count, holding back the last used.
reorganize-string.bug: Not checking the feasibility condition first.

subsets.cue: All combinations: at each element choose include or exclude (or loop from a start index).
subsets.bug: Adding the same list object to the result; add a copy (`new ArrayList<>(path)`).

subsets-ii.cue: Subsets with duplicates: sort, then skip a duplicate at the same depth (`i > start && nums[i] == nums[i-1]`).
subsets-ii.brute: Generate all and dedupe with a set: wasteful.
subsets-ii.bug: Skipping duplicates across depths, which removes valid subsets like `[2, 2]`.

permutations.cue: All orderings: build position by position with a used[] array (or swap in place).
permutations.brute: There is no faster way; n! outputs is the lower bound.

follow.a: Sort and skip `nums[i] == nums[i-1] && !used[i-1]`.

combination-sum.cue: Reusable candidates summing to a target: recurse staying on the same index, prune when the sum exceeds the target.
combination-sum.brute: Generate all multisets: exponential without pruning.
combination-sum.bug: Restarting from index 0 each call, which produces permutations of the same combination.

combination-sum-ii.cue: Each candidate used once, duplicates in input: sort, move to `i + 1`, skip same-depth duplicates.
combination-sum-ii.bug: Deduping across depths instead of within the same depth.

letter-combinations-of-a-phone-number.cue: Cartesian product of choices: one recursion level per digit.
letter-combinations-of-a-phone-number.brute: Iterative BFS building strings works too.

palindrome-partitioning.cue: Split points: try every palindromic prefix, recurse on the rest.
palindrome-partitioning.brute: Check palindromes repeatedly; precompute an `isPal[i][j]` table to save time.
edge: The whole string is a palindrome
palindrome-partitioning.bug: Not precomputing palindromes, which repeats the same checks.

word-search.cue: Path in a grid without reusing cells: DFS with a visited mark and undo.
edge: Word longer than the number of cells
word-search.bug: Not restoring the cell after DFS, so later paths see it as used.

n-queens.cue: Place one queen per row; check column and both diagonals in O(1) with sets (`r - c` and `r + c`).
n-queens.brute: Check the whole board for each placement: O(n) per check.
n-queens.bug: Wrong diagonal keys: `r - c` for one diagonal, `r + c` for the other.

number-of-islands.cue: Count connected regions in a grid: DFS/BFS from each unvisited land cell (or union-find).
number-of-islands.brute: There is no simpler approach; each cell must be seen.
number-of-islands.bug: Deep recursion on a large all-land grid can overflow the stack; mention BFS as the safe option.

follow.q: Islands added one at a time?
follow.a: Union-find with an island counter: near O(1) per addition.

max-area-of-island.cue: Connected-component size: DFS returning the count of cells.
max-area-of-island.bug: Counting a cell twice by marking it visited only after recursing.

clone-graph.cue: Deep copy of a graph with cycles: DFS/BFS with a map original→copy.
clone-graph.brute: There is no meaningful brute force.
edge: A single node with no neighbours
clone-graph.bug: Creating the copy after recursing into neighbours, so cycles recurse forever. Put it in the map first.

rotting-oranges.cue: Spreading from many sources at once, minimum time: multi-source BFS.
rotting-oranges.brute: Simulate minute by minute scanning the grid: O((m·n)²).
rotting-oranges.bug: Counting minutes per orange instead of per BFS level.

01-matrix.cue: Distance to the nearest 0 for every cell: multi-source BFS starting from all zeros.
01-matrix.bug: Starting BFS from the ones instead of the zeros.

course-schedule.cue: Prerequisites = directed graph; can you finish everything? Detect a cycle (Kahn's topological sort or DFS colours).
course-schedule.bug: Using a single visited set in DFS; you need three states (unvisited, visiting, done) to find back edges.

follow.q: Which courses are in the cycle?
follow.a: With DFS colours, keep the recursion stack and print it when you hit a 'visiting' node.

course-schedule-ii.cue: Produce the order: Kahn's algorithm, the output order is the queue pop order.
course-schedule-ii.bug: Returning a partial order when a cycle exists; check that the order holds n courses.

pacific-atlantic-water-flow.cue: "Can reach the edge" from every cell is expensive; reverse it: BFS uphill from each ocean's border.
pacific-atlantic-water-flow.brute: DFS from every cell to both oceans: O((m·n)²).
pacific-atlantic-water-flow.bug: Running the search downhill from every cell instead of uphill from the oceans.

surrounded-regions.cue: Regions not touching the border get flipped: mark everything connected to the border first, flip the rest.
surrounded-regions.brute: Check every region for border contact: same complexity, messier.
surrounded-regions.bug: Flipping while searching instead of marking the safe cells first.

word-ladder.cue: Shortest transformation sequence = shortest path in an unweighted graph: BFS over words.
word-ladder.bug: Building the full word graph upfront (O(N²·L)); generate neighbours by changing one letter, or use wildcard buckets.

follow.a: BFS to build parent links by level, then DFS back from endWord (Word Ladder II).

is-graph-bipartite.cue: Two-colour the graph: BFS/DFS assigning alternating colours; a conflict means not bipartite.
edge: Disconnected graph (start from every uncoloured node)
is-graph-bipartite.bug: Only starting from node 0, which misses other components.

shortest-path-in-binary-matrix.cue: Shortest path in a grid with equal step cost: BFS with 8 directions.
shortest-path-in-binary-matrix.bug: Marking cells visited when popped instead of when pushed, which adds duplicates to the queue.

network-delay-time.cue: Single-source shortest path with non-negative weights: Dijkstra; the answer is the largest distance.
edge: Several edges between the same pair
network-delay-time.bug: Not skipping stale heap entries (`if (d > dist[u]) continue`).

cheapest-flights-within-k-stops.cue: Shortest path with a limit on edges: Bellman-Ford for k + 1 rounds (or BFS by stops).
cheapest-flights-within-k-stops.brute: DFS over all paths up to k stops: exponential.
cheapest-flights-within-k-stops.bug: Relaxing from the array you are updating in the same round, which lets a path use more edges than allowed. Copy it first.

min-cost-to-connect-all-points.cue: Connect all points with minimum total edge cost: a minimum spanning tree (Prim's on the dense graph).
min-cost-to-connect-all-points.brute: Kruskal over all n² edges: O(n² log n).
min-cost-to-connect-all-points.bug: Using Kruskal with all edges sorted when Prim's O(n²) without a heap is better for dense graphs.

redundant-connection.cue: Find the edge that creates a cycle in an undirected graph: union-find; the first edge whose ends are already joined.
redundant-connection.brute: Remove each edge and check connectivity: O(n²).
edge: Several candidates: return the last in input order
redundant-connection.bug: Union-find without path compression or union by rank, then claiming O(α(n)) complexity.

number-of-provinces.cue: Count connected components from an adjacency matrix: DFS or union-find.
number-of-provinces.bug: Iterating only over the upper triangle and missing connections.

accounts-merge.cue: Merge records that share any email: union-find over emails (or a graph plus DFS).
accounts-merge.brute: Compare every pair of accounts repeatedly until nothing changes: O(n²·k) per round.
accounts-merge.bug: Merging by name instead of by shared email.

alien-dictionary.cue: Ordering constraints between letters from adjacent words: build edges, then topological sort.
edge: A word followed by its own prefix is invalid (`abc` before `ab`)
alien-dictionary.bug: Comparing all pairs of words instead of adjacent ones, or adding edges after the first differing letter.

swim-in-rising-water.cue: Minimise the maximum height along a path: Dijkstra on the max-edge value (or binary search the time plus BFS).
swim-in-rising-water.brute: Try every time t with a BFS: O(n² · n²).
swim-in-rising-water.bug: Summing heights like a normal shortest path instead of taking the maximum.

climbing-stairs.cue: Ways to reach step n using steps of 1 or 2: ways(n) = ways(n−1) + ways(n−2).

house-robber.cue: Choose non-adjacent elements to maximise the sum: `dp[i] = max(dp[i−1], dp[i−2] + nums[i])`.
house-robber.brute: Try all subsets of non-adjacent houses: O(2^n).
house-robber.bug: Greedy picking of the largest values, which fails on `[2, 1, 1, 2]`.

house-robber-ii.cue: Circular street: run House Robber twice, excluding the first house, then excluding the last.
house-robber-ii.bug: Returning 0 for a single house because both ranges are empty.

coin-change.cue: Fewest coins for an amount, unlimited supply: unbounded knapsack, `dp[a] = min(dp[a − c] + 1)`.
coin-change.brute: Recursion over every coin choice: exponential.
edge: A coin larger than the amount
coin-change.bug: Greedy largest-coin-first, which fails for coins `[1, 3, 4]`, amount 6.

follow.a: That is Coin Change II: loop coins outside amounts so combinations are counted once.

longest-increasing-subsequence.cue: Not contiguous, increasing: O(n²) DP, or patience sorting with binary search for O(n log n).
edge: Strictly increasing (equal values do not extend)
longest-increasing-subsequence.bug: Presenting the `tails` array as the actual subsequence; it only has the right length.

follow.a: Keep a predecessor index for each element and rebuild from the end.

word-break.cue: Can the string be split into dictionary words? `dp[i]` = prefix of length i is breakable.
word-break.brute: Recursion trying every prefix: exponential without memoisation.
edge: Words that are prefixes of others
word-break.bug: Not putting the dictionary in a `HashSet`, which makes each lookup O(words).

decode-ways.cue: Count decodings of a digit string: like climbing stairs, a 1-digit or 2-digit step when valid.
decode-ways.bug: Treating a `0` as a valid single digit.

partition-equal-subset-sum.cue: Split into two equal sums = subset with sum total/2: 0/1 knapsack on a boolean array.
partition-equal-subset-sum.bug: Iterating sums upwards in the 1-D array, which reuses an item; go from high to low.

maximum-product-subarray.cue: Product, not sum: keep both the max and the min ending here, because a negative flips them.
maximum-product-subarray.bug: Updating max before computing min with the old max; use temporaries.

longest-palindromic-substring.cue: Expand around each centre (2n − 1 centres) for O(n²) with O(1) space.
longest-palindromic-substring.bug: Only expanding around single characters, which misses even-length palindromes.

follow.a: Manacher's algorithm; naming it is usually enough.

palindromic-substrings.cue: Count palindromes by expanding around every centre.

unique-paths.cue: Grid with right/down moves: `dp[r][c] = dp[r−1][c] + dp[r][c−1]`, or the combination C(m+n−2, m−1).
unique-paths.bug: Overflow when computing the combination with factorials; multiply and divide step by step using `long`.

longest-common-subsequence.cue: Two strings, compare prefixes: match → diagonal + 1, else max of left and up.
longest-common-subsequence.brute: All subsequences of one string: O(2^n).
longest-common-subsequence.bug: Off-by-one: use a table of size (m+1)×(n+1) with an empty-prefix row and column.

edit-distance.cue: Minimum insert/delete/replace: `dp[i][j]` from three neighbours plus the diagonal when characters match.
edge: One string empty (length of the other)
edit-distance.bug: Forgetting the base row and column (i deletions, j insertions).

target-sum.cue: Assign + or − to reach a target: it reduces to counting subsets with sum (total + target) / 2.
target-sum.bug: Not checking `|target| > total` before indexing the array.

coin-change-ii.cue: Count combinations (not permutations): loop coins in the outer loop, amounts in the inner.
coin-change-ii.bug: Swapping the loops, which counts permutations.

interleaving-string.cue: Can s3 interleave s1 and s2? `dp[i][j]` = first i of s1 and first j of s2 form the first i + j of s3.

distinct-subsequences.cue: Count ways t appears as a subsequence of s: match → use it or skip it, else skip.
distinct-subsequences.bug: Integer overflow in intermediate counts; the problem bounds the answer, but intermediate values may need `long`.

longest-increasing-path-in-a-matrix.cue: Longest path in a DAG implied by strictly increasing values: DFS with memoisation.
longest-increasing-path-in-a-matrix.brute: DFS from every cell without memo: exponential.
longest-increasing-path-in-a-matrix.bug: Using a visited set; strict increase already prevents cycles, so memoisation is all you need.

burst-balloons.cue: Interval DP: choose the last balloon to burst in each range so its neighbours are fixed.
burst-balloons.bug: Choosing the first balloon to burst, which leaves neighbours unknown.

best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock-with-coo.cue: Stock problems with rules = a small state machine (hold, sold, rest) per day.
best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock-with-coo.bug: Allowing a buy the day after a sell.

jump-game.cue: Can you reach the end? Track the furthest reachable index.
jump-game.brute: DP or BFS over positions: O(n²).
jump-game.bug: Continuing after `i > furthest`; you are already stuck.

jump-game-ii.cue: Minimum jumps: BFS by levels in one pass; each level is the range reachable with k jumps.
edge: Already able to reach the end from index 0
jump-game-ii.bug: Counting a jump at the last index.

gas-station.cue: If total gas ≥ total cost a solution exists; restart after any prefix whose tank goes negative.
gas-station.bug: Not being able to justify why no station inside a failed prefix can be the start.

hand-of-straights.cue: Form consecutive groups: always start a group at the smallest remaining card (TreeMap of counts).
hand-of-straights.bug: Starting groups at arbitrary cards instead of the smallest.

partition-labels.cue: Each part must contain every occurrence of its letters: record each letter's last index, cut when you reach the furthest one.
edge: All distinct letters (every part has size 1)
partition-labels.bug: Cutting at the current letter's last index instead of the running maximum.

valid-parenthesis-string.cue: With `*` wildcards, track the range [low, high] of possible open counts.
valid-parenthesis-string.bug: Not clamping low at 0, or not failing when high goes negative.

task-scheduler.cue: Idle time is driven by the most frequent task: `(maxCount − 1) · (n + 1) + tasksWithMaxCount`, at least the number of tasks.
task-scheduler.brute: Simulate with a heap: O(total time · log 26).
edge: Several tasks tied for the maximum
task-scheduler.bug: Forgetting the `max(formula, tasks.length)` case when there are many distinct tasks.

merge-intervals.cue: Overlapping intervals: sort by start, then extend or append.
merge-intervals.bug: Setting the end to the new interval's end instead of `max(end, newEnd)`, which shrinks contained intervals.

follow.a: Keep them in a `TreeMap` by start and merge with the floor and ceiling neighbours.

insert-interval.cue: Sorted, non-overlapping list plus one new interval: copy those before, merge the overlaps, copy those after.
insert-interval.brute: Append and run Merge Intervals: O(n log n).
edge: Insert at the start or end
insert-interval.bug: Off-by-one on the touching condition (`end >= newStart`).

non-overlapping-intervals.cue: Minimum removals = n − maximum non-overlapping set: sort by end and keep greedily.
edge: Touching intervals do not overlap here
non-overlapping-intervals.bug: Sorting by start without handling which interval to keep.

meeting-rooms-ii.cue: Maximum number of overlapping intervals: sort starts and ends separately (or a min-heap of end times).
meeting-rooms-ii.brute: Check every time point: depends on the time range.
edge: A meeting ending when another starts can reuse the room
meeting-rooms-ii.bug: Using `<` vs `<=` wrongly at touching end and start times.

follow.q: Which room does each meeting get?
follow.a: A min-heap of (endTime, roomId) and a free-rooms heap (Meeting Rooms III).

minimum-number-of-arrows-to-burst-balloo.cue: Interval stabbing: sort by end, shoot at the end of the first, skip all it covers.
edge: Large values: compare without subtraction overflow
minimum-number-of-arrows-to-burst-balloo.bug: Comparator `a[1] - b[1]` overflows for values near `Integer.MIN/MAX`; use `Integer.compare`.

single-number.cue: Every element twice except one: XOR everything, the pairs cancel.
single-number.brute: A hash set or counts: O(n) space.
single-number.bug: Not being able to explain why: `a ^ a = 0` and `a ^ 0 = a`, and XOR is commutative.

follow.q: Every element three times except one?
follow.a: Count each bit modulo 3.

counting-bits.cue: Bits of i from smaller numbers: `bits[i] = bits[i >> 1] + (i & 1)`.
counting-bits.brute: Count bits for every number: O(n log n).
counting-bits.bug: Recomputing from scratch for each i.

number-of-1-bits.cue: Count set bits: `n &= n − 1` clears the lowest set bit each step.
edge: Treat input as unsigned in Java (negative ints)
number-of-1-bits.bug: Using `>>` on a negative number, which loops forever; use `>>>` or the `n & (n − 1)` trick.

reverse-bits.cue: Shift the result left and the input right 32 times, moving one bit each time.
reverse-bits.brute: Convert to a string and reverse.
reverse-bits.bug: Using `>>` instead of `>>>` on the input.

missing-number.cue: 0..n with one missing: XOR of indices and values, or `n(n+1)/2 − sum`.
missing-number.brute: Sort and scan: O(n log n). Hash set: O(n) space.
missing-number.bug: Sum overflow for large n; XOR avoids it.

sum-of-two-integers.cue: Add without `+`: XOR is the sum without carry, `(a & b) << 1` is the carry; repeat until the carry is 0.
sum-of-two-integers.brute: There is no other approach without arithmetic operators.
sum-of-two-integers.bug: Assuming it loops forever on negatives; in Java the carry shifts out after 32 bits.

powx-n.cue: Fast exponentiation: square the base, halve the exponent.

happy-number.cue: A repeating process that may cycle: detect the cycle with a set or Floyd's slow/fast pointers.

plus-one.cue: Add with carry from the last digit; only all-9s grows the array.
plus-one.bug: Not handling the extra leading digit.
